Fetch a CVM open-data table

Source: R/api-cvm-fetch.R
cvm_fetch.Rd

Single public entry point for any table of any dataset covered by the package. Selects the right file, downloads (or serves from the cache or the parquet mirror), parses, applies the schema-declared transformations, filters by issuer and period, and returns a tibble carrying provenance attributes.

Usage

cvm_fetch(
  dataset,
  table,
  cnpj = NULL,
  ticker = NULL,
  year = NULL,
  from = NULL,
  to = NULL,
  as_of = NULL,
  basis = NULL,
  reading = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  on_error = "abort",
  validate = "strict",
  ...
)

Arguments

dataset

Short dataset id (e.g. "cad", "dfp").

table

Snake-case table name (e.g. "companhias", "bpa"). For tables published in individual and consolidated variants, table is the concept name and basis selects the variant(s).

cnpj

Optional character vector of issuer CNPJs, with or without punctuation ("00.000.000/0001-91" or "00000000000191"). Only CNPJs are accepted: a CVM code or a company name aborts with cvmdata_error_input. NULL (default) keeps every issuer. A CNPJ absent from the table yields zero rows for it, silently.

ticker

Optional character vector of B3 trading codes ("PETR4", "BBAS3"). Each ticker is resolved to its issuer CNPJ through fca/valor_mobiliario (read from the same source) and then filtered like cnpj; the two arguments combine. The lookup reads every yearly FCA file that carries trading codes (2018 onwards), so the code of a company that has since left the exchange still resolves, for any year. A ticker absent from every file aborts with cvmdata_error_input; so does a ticker that maps to more than one issuer (pass cnpj instead).

year

Integer vector of years to fetch, as the CVM publishes them (one file per year). NULL (default) fetches the latest available year. Must be NULL for datasets with temporal_partitioning: none (e.g. CAD), and cannot be combined with from/to. Years the table is not published for are refused before any download: years before the table's first year, and years from which the CVM publishes its CSV with the header only (fca/departamento_acionistas from 2024, after Resolução CVM 59/2021 revoked the block). For such a table, year = NULL warns (cvmdata_warn_empty_upstream): the mirror returns the last year with content, the portal returns the latest file, which has zero rows.

from, to

Optional period bounds, both required together, as complete dates ("YYYY-MM-DD" strings or Date scalars). Rows are kept when the document's reference date (dt_refer or data_referencia) falls inside [from, to]; the yearly files read are the years spanned by the interval. Incomplete dates ("2024", "2024-06") are rejected. Cannot be combined with year, and do not apply to snapshot tables such as CAD.

as_of

Optional complete date ("YYYY-MM-DD" or Date) for registry tables only (cad/companhias): keeps the registrations in force on that date, i.e. registered on or before it and not cancelled by it. The rows are the register as the CVM publishes it today, not a reconstruction of the past. See the section Company register. Passing it for any other table aborts.

basis

Individual ("ind"), consolidated ("con") or both (c("ind", "con")) financial statements. Required for tables that publish the two variants (bpa, bpp, dre, dra, dfc_md, dfc_mi, dmpl, dva): there is no default, because many issuers file only individual statements. Those tables always carry a basis column in the result, even when a single value was requested. Must be NULL for every other table; passing it aborts.

reading

Which reading of each fiscal exercise to return, for the DFP and ITR statement tables (the ones with ordem_exerc): "original" (the figures the issuer filed for the exercise, the ÚLTIMO rows of that year's file), "restated" (the comparative figures for the same exercise in the following year's file, the PENÚLTIMO rows there) or c("original", "restated"), which stacks both. NULL (default) returns each year's file as the CVM publishes it, ÚLTIMO and PENÚLTIMO rows together, without a reading column. When set, year names the exercises and the following year's files are read as needed; the result carries a reading column. See the section Readings of an exercise. Must be NULL for tables without ordem_exerc; passing it aborts.

source

One of "mirror" (parquet via DuckDB) or "cvm" (CVM Open Data Portal). NULL (default) resolves to the active backend via cvm_source_get().

on_error

One of "abort" (default), "warn" or "silent". Controls behaviour on HTTP failures when several yearly files are read (year with more than one element, or a from/to window spanning several years). With "warn", the failed years are skipped and a cvmdata_warn_partial_failure warning lists them; with "silent", they are skipped silently; with "abort", the first failure aborts the call. Total failure always aborts.

validate

One of "strict" (default), "warn" or "skip". Controls schema validation strictness at parse time.

...

Reserved for forward compatibility. Currently no extra arguments are accepted; passing any aborts with cvmdata_error_input.

Value

A tibble of class cvm_tbl carrying the provenance attributes source, fetched_at, group, dataset, table and package_version.

Details

Column names, categorical values and free-text fields are preserved in Portuguese exactly as published by CVM (snake_case minúsculo).

Readings of an exercise

Every yearly DFP and ITR statement file carries two columns of figures per account: ordem_exerc = "ÚLTIMO", the exercise the file is about, and ordem_exerc = "PENÚLTIMO", the comparative the issuer presented for the previous exercise. The comparative is often not the figure originally filed: issuers restate it after a change of accounting policy, an error or a reorganisation (about a third of the issuers in the DFP, measured on the 2023 file against the 2022 one), and the restated figure is the one later statements build on. With reading, cvm_fetch() reads the exercise by its own year and labels each row:

  • "original": the ÚLTIMO rows of the file of year.

  • "restated": the PENÚLTIMO rows of the file of year + 1, read in addition to (or instead of) the file of year. Rows are returned as the CVM publishes them, so dt_refer and versao are those of the following year's document and dt_fim_exerc (and dt_ini_exerc) identify the exercise the figure belongs to. An exercise whose following year's file is not published yet has no restated reading; the call says so and returns what exists. When the file exists but the issuer has not filed in it yet, its restated rows are simply absent.

The two readings of an exercise pair on the issuer, the exercise dates, cd_conta and, in dmpl, coluna_df. Either reading can be absent for an issuer (it stopped filing, or started filing in the following year), and a restated figure can be 0 where the issuer presented no comparative at all, as the banks did for 2024 on the individual basis after adopting CMN Resolution 4,966 in 2025. In the ITR, the comparative of the balance sheet (bpa, bpp) is the previous year end, not the previous year's quarter, so the restated reading of an ITR balance sheet is the year-end balance as the following year's quarterly filings present it.

With from/to, the window applies to the exercise end (dt_fim_exerc) rather than to the document date, so an exercise's two readings stay together.

Company register

cad/companhias is a single file holding today's state of every registration the CVM ever granted: companies that cancelled their registration stay in it, with sit = "CANCELADA", dt_cancel and motivo_cancel (cancellations go back to 1984 and are three quarters of the rows). Its key is (cnpj_cia, cd_cvm, tp_merc), which has two consequences for joins:

  • A few dozen CNPJs hold two registrations (a company that cancelled and registered again years later under a new CVM code). These are distinct registrations and the package keeps them apart.

  • About a hundred registrations are repeated in two or three rows that differ only in tp_merc (the markets the company is admitted to: exchange, organised OTC, non-organised OTC). Every other column is identical. A join on cnpj_cia alone duplicates those companies. The package returns the file as published; for one row per registration, drop the market before joining, e.g. dplyr::distinct(reg, cnpj_cia, cd_cvm, .keep_all = TRUE). tp_merc is empty for almost every cancelled company, so filtering on it discards delisted companies.

as_of answers "which companies were registered on date X" from the registration and cancellation dates of each registration, which is what a survivorship-free universe needs. The rows it returns are still today's: a company registered in 2012 and cancelled in 2017 is part of the 2015 universe, but its row says "CANCELADA", because the CVM does not publish past states of the register (the file only records when the current value of each field started). The yearly fca/geral file is the CVM's own picture of a company in a given year (name, registration situation, category, issuer situation).

Arguments by table

Which arguments apply depends on the table. The rules below are generated from the package's table schemas, the same ones the argument checks read, for the 74 tables in 8 datasets. An argument passed to a table it does not apply to aborts with cvmdata_error_input before anything is downloaded; nothing is silently ignored.

  • year and from/to: every table published one file per year. Not for cad: companhias, a single snapshot. A year before the table's first year is refused (a from/to window is cut to it instead). Most tables start with their dataset; these start later: dfp/composicao_capital (2020), fre/acao_entregue (2023), fre/administrador_PCD (2023), fre/administrador_declaracao_genero (2023), fre/administrador_declaracao_raca (2023), fre/empregado_PCD (2023), fre/empregado_local_declaracao_genero (2023), fre/empregado_local_declaracao_raca (2023), fre/empregado_local_faixa_etaria (2023), fre/empregado_posicao_declaracao_genero (2023), fre/empregado_posicao_declaracao_raca (2023), fre/empregado_posicao_faixa_etaria (2023), fre/empregado_posicao_local (2023), fre/mercado_estrangeiro (2019), fre/remuneracao_acao (2023), fre/remuneracao_variavel (2023), fre/titular_valor_mobiliario (2018), fre/titulo_exterior (2016), itr/composicao_capital (2020).

  • Years from which the CVM publishes the file with its header only are refused too: fca/departamento_acionistas (2024).

  • basis: required, with no default, in dfp and itr: bpa, bpp, dfc_md, dfc_mi, dmpl, dra, dre, dva. Refused in every other table.

  • reading: only in dfp and itr: bpa, bpp, dfc_md, dfc_mi, dmpl, dra, dre, dva (the tables with ordem_exerc).

  • as_of: only in cad: companhias.

  • cvm_versions(): every table except cad: companhias; cgvn, dfp, fca, fre and itr: submissao; ipe: ipe; vlmo: consolidado, submissao, which already return every row the CVM publishes.

Filing versions

When a detail table carries several filings for the same issuer and reference date, only the last one delivered is kept, ranked by receipt date, then CVM document id, then versao. The version number alone is not a filing key: the CVM index can list two filings under the same version, or a later filing under a lower one.

The submissao table of each dataset is the filing index and is not collapsed: it returns one row per delivery, re-filings included, with the receipt date (dt_receb or data_entrega), the document id (id_doc, id_documento or protocolo_entrega) and versao. The current filing of an issuer and reference date is the last row by that order; joining submissao to a detail table on the issuer and reference date alone matches every delivery.

Tables of datasets with a submissao index are checked against it before returning. In DFP and ITR tables, rows the CVM file holds twice are dropped (cvmdata_warn_duplicate_filing); copies that differ in vl_conta are kept (cvmdata_warn_conflicting_filing). A table holding an earlier filing than the last delivery keeps the CVM numbers and warns (cvmdata_warn_stale_filing). Set options(cvmdata.check_filings = FALSE) to skip these checks.

See also

Other fetchers: cvm_versions()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # interactive()
# CAD: single snapshot, no year, no basis
issuers <- cvm_fetch("cad", "companhias")

# Registrations in force at the end of 2015 (survivorship-free
# universe), one row per registration
u2015 <- cvm_fetch("cad", "companhias", as_of = "2015-12-31")
u2015 <- dplyr::distinct(u2015, cnpj_cia, cd_cvm, .keep_all = TRUE)

# A delisted company by its former ticker
gol <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "dre", ticker = "GOLL4", year = 2019, basis = "con")

# DFP balance sheet (assets), individual statements, latest year,
# one issuer by CNPJ
bb <- cvm_fetch("dfp", "bpa", cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91", basis = "ind")

# Both bases, 2022 to 2024, issuer by B3 ticker
petr <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "dre",
  ticker = "PETR4",
  year = 2022:2024,
  basis = c("ind", "con")
)

# ITR by reference date: the quarters of the first half of 2024
h1 <- cvm_fetch(
  "itr", "bpa",
  from = "2024-01-01", to = "2024-06-30",
  basis = "con"
)

# Exercise 2022 as originally filed and as restated in the 2023
# file, side by side in a `reading` column
pssa <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "bpa",
  ticker = "PSSA3",
  year = 2022,
  basis = "con",
  reading = c("original", "restated")
)
}
